digest_markdown:
• [1] A supply chain attack on SolarWinds' Orion IT monitoring system, used by over 30,000 organizations, was compromised by hackers, allowing them to deliver backdoor malware in a software update. [1]
• [1] A compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release was published to the Python Package Index (PyPI) and distributed through official container images, allowing hackers to steal authentication material across developer tools, AI applications, cloud environments, browsers, and infrastructure. [2]
• [2] A GhostAction supply chain attack compromised 3,325 secrets, exposing tokens and keys across widely used platforms including PyPI, npm, DockerHub, GitHub, AWS, and Cloudflare. [3]
• [3] A new wave of the GhostAction supply chain campaign compromised 772 public GitHub repositories, using fake GitHub Actions workflow files to steal credentials from CI/CD environments. [4]
• [4] The GhostAction supply chain campaign uses stolen GitHub account access to add malicious workflows under the victim's own identity, making it difficult to detect during a quick code review. [4]
